subject: Approve: Aperture Health — Ramp Incentive Clearance (VP/CFO required)
messages:
From: Lena Torres <lena.torres@aperturehealth.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@aperturehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Revised pricing request — 2yr ramp incentive and term structure

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the call this morning. Aperture wants to move forward contingent on a commercial structure that helps us get through the first-year budget constraints while aligning to a multi-year commitment. High level ask: a two-year ramp incentive with deeper concession in Year 1 (to help with implementation & POC costs), phasing up to standard list rates by Year 2.

Key points from our side:
- Year 1 blended effective rate target: ~40% off list for the first 6 months, then 25% off for the remainder of Year 1.
- Year 2: 10–15% off list depending on usage thresholds (slab-based).
- Minimum 24-month term and a 12-month minimum commitment each year.
- Need clear audit and data residency assurances for PHI scope.

Attached is the updated SOW and expected volume profile. We can sign an SOW quickly if we get an approval on the commercial carveout.

Attachments: Aperture_SOW_Q2_v3.pdf

Looking forward — Lena
From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Lena Torres <lena.torres@aperturehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Revised pricing request — 2yr ramp incentive and term structure

Hi Lena — appreciate the clear ask and the SOW. I ran the numbers and this request is a material deviation from standard gating (discount depth > 25% in Year 1).

Short summary of what Aperture is requesting:
- 24-month term, staged discounts (deep in Q1–Q2 then step up)
- Strong commitment to 12-month minimums each year
- PHI scope with private deployment pricing implications

Marissa / Ben — looping you in for VP/CFO signoff. This would require an exception to rate-card guardrails and a short-term guarantee (we've proposed audit cadence + rollback clause). I attached my working commercial summary for internal review — AP-Commercial_Summary_v1.xlsx.

Proposed internal ask (for approval):
- Approve blended Year 1 concession up to 35% for first 6 months, then 20% through month 12 (blended ~27%).
- Year 2: 12% off list, with usage thresholds to scale pricing closer to list.
- Add a 90-day performance and security milestone — failure to meet results in step-up to list rates.
- Require legal to include a 6-month clawback on usage credits and a signed SOC2 appendix.

If you approve, I will send an updated commercial SOW and request DocuSign.

Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: MEMO: Aperture Health — commercial clearance request (summary + recommendation)

Team — short memo. Mateo has routed a pricing exception request from Aperture Health for a two-year ramp incentive. The ask materially exceeds our standard discount guardrails and touches private deployment / PHI pricing. I recommend we grant a controlled exception with the following guardrails and reporting.

Executive recommendation (approve with conditions):
- Approval: blended concession capped at 35% for the initial 6-month ramp period, stepping to 20% through month 12; Year 2 capped at 12% off list and tied to usage slabs.
- Guardrails: 12-month minimum commitment each year; quarterly usage reviews against the baseline; immediate rollback to list rates on material non-performance or security audit failure.
- Financial controls: require a 90% NRR target at renewal and a minimum ARR floor of $600k to maintain the concession for Year 2.
- Contractual asks: SOC2 appendix, audit rights, and a 6-month credit clawback.

Rationale: Aperture is strategically aligned (large enterprise healthcare footprint) and the deal yields a multi-year committed revenue stream; the structured ramp limits near-term revenue loss and preserves upside if usage accelerates. We should balance near-term concession with measurable milestones and finance oversight.

Attachments: deal_impact_model_aph.xlsx (impact model), legal redline summary included inline.

Requested approvers: Markus (CFO) & Ben (Head of Rev Ops) — please confirm or flag changes. If approved, I will instruct Legal to prepare the final SOW with the noted clauses and coordinate DocuSign.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MEMO: Aperture Health — commercial clearance request (summary + recommendation)

Marissa / team —

I reviewed the impact model and risk controls. I will approve the outlined ramp incentive on these explicit conditions:
1) We execute the SOC2 appendix and a security milestone check at 60 days.
2) Include a mandatory quarterly usage review tied to a price step-up if usage is < 75% of committed baseline for two consecutive quarters.
3) Add a 6-month clawback clause for credits and a 12-month audit right.
4) Legal to require a holdback clause of 10% of Year 1 invoice value until the 60-day security milestone is confirmed.

Once legal confirms the contract language I approve final signoff. Attaching the CFO sign-off stamp for recordkeeping.

Attachments: cfo_signoff_stamp.pdf

-Markus Klein
CFO (acting) | Redwood Inference
